theory.intro: A **composite figure** is made from simpler shapes joined together. Find its area by splitting it into rectangles and triangles and adding, or by subtracting a missing piece from a large rectangle.
facts: Area of a rectangle $=$ length $\times$ width.
For a figure made only from horizontal and vertical sides, find missing lengths by matching the total horizontal lengths in each direction and the total vertical lengths in each direction.
Area of a triangle $=$ base $\times$ perpendicular height $\div2$.
Use the same length unit and write areas in squared units.
When rectangles overlap, count the shared area only once.
steps: Split the figure into simple shapes, or show the whole shape and the piece to remove.
Work out any missing lengths and use the same length unit.
Calculate the area of each simple shape.
Add or subtract the areas as needed and write squared units.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Subtract the window area from the whole wall area.
$\begin{align*} A&=12\times7-3\times2\\ &=84-6\\ &=78\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$
(b) The missing triangle is half of the $5\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ corner rectangle.
$\begin{align*} A&=11\times7-5\times4\div2\\ &=77-10\\ &=67\text{ cm}^2 \end{align*}$

Adding both mat areas counts the shared rectangle twice. Subtract its area once.
$\begin{align*} A&=8\times5+7\times4-2\times3\\ &=40+28-6\\ &=68-6\\ &=62\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular backyard is $15.5\text{ m}$ long and $9.2\text{ m}$ wide. It contains a triangular pool with base $6\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $3.4\text{ m}$, and a square patio with side $4\text{ m}$. The pool and patio do not overlap. Find the remaining area to the nearest whole square metre.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract both occupied areas from the yard area.
$\begin{align*} A_{\text{yard}}&=15.5\times9.2\\ &=142.6\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$
$\begin{align*} A_{\text{pool}}&=6\times3.4\div2\\ &=10.2\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$
$\begin{align*} A_{\text{patio}}&=4\times4\\ &=16\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$
$\begin{align*} A&=142.6-10.2-16\\ &=116.4\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$
To the nearest whole square metre, the remaining area is $116\text{ m}^2$.

mastery.question_text:
A backyard is a rectangle with dimensions $16.5\text{ m}$ by $10.2\text{ m}$. A triangular swimming pool with a base of $7.2\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $3.5\text{ m}$ is constructed in one section, and a square patio with a side length of $4.5\text{ m}$ is paved in another. The pool and patio do not overlap.
Calculate the remaining area of the yard to the nearest whole square metre.
mastery.solution_text:
Yard area: $16.5\times10.2=168.3\text{ m}^2$.
Pool area: $7.2\times3.5\div2=12.6\text{ m}^2$.
Patio area: $4.5\times4.5=20.25\text{ m}^2$.
$A=168.3-12.6-20.25$
$=135.45\text{ m}^2$
To the nearest whole square metre, the remaining area is $135\text{ m}^2$.
